propositions: The wire history processor's request-fit check never executes on first requests because proc() only descends into ModelResponse messages, making the guard unreachable when history is [ModelRequest]

A first request with 3.6M chars of instructions against a 1M-token window was sent to the provider without any check, surfacing as LLMUnavailableError instead of ContextWindowExceededError before the call
The seam must estimate request tokens at 4 chars/token to keep enrich's window*2-char bound admissible (chars/4 estimates ~window/2 tokens; chars/2 would fail closed at window exactly)
Adding _check_request_fit to proc allows the same projection callable to check both first and subsequent requests uniformly, raising ContextWindowExceededError when estimate + reserve exceeds window
Per-op bounds remain first-line bounds; the shared seam acts as a backstop and does not modify or remove existing per-op bounds
The error type matches errors.py's documented contract (request-terms: system/user/tool content) and is already caught by 13 broad LLMError handlers
